extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners and applicants (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for Continued Prosecution Applications (CPAs), continuation, divisional, and continuation-in-part applications including inventorship, benefit/priority claims, document entry, and examiner handling. Focused on how examiners should evaluate and process these filings and what applicants must provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance of CPA request with 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) must comply with 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2); otherwise no CPA has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the designated form paragraph to inform applicant that a request for a CPA is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2) and therefore no CPA has been established; insert filing date and application number in brackets as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for statement deleting named inventor(s) in CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement requesting deletion of the name(s) of person(s) who are not inventors in a continuation or divisional application must be signed by persons authorized pursuant to 37 CFR 1.33(b) to sign an amendment in the continuation or divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, the statement must be signed by: (1) a patent practitioner of record under 37 CFR 1.32(b); (2) a patent practitioner not of record acting under 37 CFR 1.34; or (3) the applicant (37 CFR 1.42). For applications filed prior to Sept 16, 2012, additional signatories (e.g., assignees, all applicants) are allowed per 37 CFR provisions. Unless specified, papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity must be signed by a patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of inventor-deletion statement in CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should acknowledge receipt of a statement filed with a CPA requesting deletion of named inventor(s) in the first Office action in the CPA by using form paragraph 2.32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.32; after the first Office action is mailed send the application file to OPAP to revise records to reflect change of inventorship. Applicants should not request a corrected filing receipt showing inventorship change until after examiner's Office action acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive entity carryover from prior application into CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventive entity of the CPA will be the same as the inventive entity of the prior application unless the CPA request is accompanied by or includes on filing a statement requesting deletion of a person who is not an inventor, or a request under 37 CFR 1.48 is filed to change inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transmittal letter or new oath naming an inventor not named in the prior application will be placed in the file but does not change inventive entity absent a request under 37 CFR 1.48 (including required fee). For continuing applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, the oath/declaration must comply with the revised 35 U.S.C. 115 wording (origination and authorization statements and 18 U.S.C. 1001 penalty acknowledgement). Failure to file 1.48 may result in rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding a new inventor to CPA requires 37 CFR 1.48
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CPA identifies an inventor not named in the prior application, a request to add an inventor must be in the form of a request under 37 CFR 1.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.33 to notify applicant when an inventor is identified in the CPA but no 1.48 request was filed. Otherwise, inventorship in the CPA remains the same as in the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA request constitutes specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a CPA is a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120 to every application assigned the application number identified in the request; the recitation of the prior application number in the CPA request satisfies the specific reference requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further amendment to the specification or reference in the application data sheet is required by 35 U.S.C. 120 or 37 CFR 1.78(d) to identify the prior application(s). In chains of CPAs, a specific reference to a CPA by application number constitutes a specific reference to every CPA and the original non-continued prosecution application assigned that number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to reference CPA when seeking benefit in later-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant in an application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) seeks to claim the benefit of a CPA under 35 U.S.C. 120 or 121, 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2) requires a reference to the CPA by application number in an application data sheet or (for apps filed before Sept 16, 2012) in the first sentence of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.78(d)(4) treats identification by application number as identification of every application assigned that application number; thus referencing a CPA in a chain will constitute reference to every CPA in that chain and the non-continued prosecution application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to first sentence(s) of specification in CPA not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to the first sentence(s) of the specification to provide a reference to the prior application or to label the CPA as a continuation/divisional will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.34 to inform applicant that the amendment requesting that the specification be amended to refer to the present CPA as a continuation or divisional of the prior application has not been entered and will not be entered. Provide the filing date and application number in the form paragraph brackets as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) carry over to CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) made in a parent application will automatically carry over to a CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should note that provisional-applicant-specific rules apply (provisionals are not entitled to benefit of other applications) and check bib-data sheet entries for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer in parent application carries over to CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed in the parent application carries over to a CPA because the CPA retains the same application number as the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not want the terminal disclaimer to carry over, applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with the required fee requesting withdrawal of the terminal disclaimer from the CPA. See MPEP § 1490 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover of prior election to CPA only if conditions A–D met
rubrics_metrics.description: An election in reply to a restriction requirement made in the prior application carries over to the CPA only if: (A) the CPA is designated as a continuation or is not designated (i.e., not designated as a divisional); (B) there was an express election by the applicant in reply to the restriction requirement in the prior application; (C) the CPA presents claims drawn only to invention(s) claimed in the prior application; and (D) the CPA does not contain an indication that a shift in election is desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where all conditions are met, the examiner’s first action should repeat the prior restriction requirement to the extent still applicable and include a statement that prosecution is being continued on the invention elected and prosecuted by applicant in the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments and IDS timing for CPA filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to file information disclosure statements (IDS) and preliminary amendments at the time of filing a CPA because submissions after the first Office action may not be entered or may delay prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All IDS complying with 37 CFR 1.98 filed before mailing of the first Office action will be considered. Submission of an IDS after the first Office action may delay prosecution. A preliminary amendment filed after the filing date of the CPA could be denied entry under 37 CFR 1.115 if it unduly interferes with preparation of a first Office action. Applicants may request a three‑month suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(b) at the time of filing a CPA if they need more time to prepare preliminary amendments or IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits and declarations from parent automatically become part of CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits and declarations (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131, 1.132) filed during prosecution of the parent nonprovisional application automatically become part of the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No copy of the original affidavit or declaration filed in the parent nonprovisional application need be filed in the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of confidentiality for CPAs under 35 U.S.C. 122
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA is construed to include a waiver of confidentiality by the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent members of the public entitled under 37 CFR 1.14 to access the prior application may be given similar access to the CPA and related application file information (37 CFR 1.53(d)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides public access to copies of and information concerning the prior application and any continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) consistent with Office rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy content and filing date representation for CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of a CPA will consist of a copy of the most recent non-continued prosecution application in the chain of CPAs; the filing date of the CPA will be shown as the filing date of that most recent non-continued prosecution application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copies are prepared by the Certification Section of the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO/SB/29 for filing CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/29, 'For Design Applications Only: Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) Request Transmittal,' may be used by applicant for filing a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is available on www.uspto.gov/PatentForms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation application requirements (no new matter; common inventor; benefit claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation application is for invention(s) disclosed in a prior-filed copending nonprovisional application and must not include subject matter that would constitute new matter if submitted as an amendment to the parent application; the continuation must include at least one inventor named in the prior-filed application and must claim the benefit of the prior application under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuation may be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or 1.53(d) for design applications). See 37 CFR 1.78 and MPEP § 211 for additional requirements, and ensure disclosure does not introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA filing timing and completeness requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) must be filed prior to payment of the issue fee unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c) is granted in the prior application; a continuation or divisional may only be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) if the prior application is a nonprovisional design application that is complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b) and the prior application contains an application data sheet indicating inventor name, residence, and mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CPAs filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, the oath/declaration may be excepted for completeness purposes. Use form paragraph 2.05 to remind applicants of possible continuation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-in-part (CIP) definition and filing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation-in-part application repeats some substantial portion or all of a prior-filed application and adds matter not disclosed in the prior application; a CIP must be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), must claim the benefit of the prior under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c), and CANNOT be filed as a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application claiming the benefit of a provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) should not be called a CIP of the provisional. The Office need not determine 35 U.S.C. 120/35 U.S.C. 112(a) entitlement unless the earlier filing date is relied upon in a proceeding before the Office. Use form paragraph 2.06 to inform applicants of possible CIP status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for claiming benefit of earlier nonprovisional in alleged CIP
rubrics_metrics.description: An alleged CIP should be permitted to claim the benefit of an earlier nonprovisional application if it complies with other requirements of 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78, such as: (A) same inventor or at least one common joint inventor; (B) filed before patenting, abandonment, or termination of proceedings on the first application; and (C) contains or is amended to contain a specific reference to the earlier filed application (ADS for apps on/after Sept 16, 2012; first sentence(s) or ADS for apps before that date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 211 et seq. for more information. A petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim may be required in some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties re: notation of prior application data on bib-data sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must review identifying data of all prior applications for which benefits are claimed to ensure accuracy and that the data is provided in an ADS (for apps filed on/after Sept 16, 2012) or in the first sentence(s) of the specification or ADS (for apps filed before that date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior application data errors exist, technical support staff can correct Patent Data Portal entries and republish bib-data sheets; applicant errors should be corrected via corrected or supplemental ADS or amendment. See MPEP §§ 601.05, 211.02(a). Inclusion of prior application information on the bib-data sheet does not automatically indicate entitlement to benefit; check MPEP §§ 213.01, 2136.03, 2154.01(b), and §306 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application benefit notation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to a prior provisional application, the prior provisional should not list earlier domestic or foreign applications as having been claimed by the provisional (a provisional is not entitled to the benefit of or priority to another application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure provisional application data is properly handled on the bib-data sheet; do not reflect earlier applications that the provisional itself purports to claim benefit from.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority notation and examiner actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreign application listed on the oath/declaration or ADS is not listed on the bib-data sheet and the foreign priority claim is proper, the examiner should provide the foreign application number, country, and filing date to the Legal Instrument Examiner for correction; if applications are listed on the bib-data sheet but filed in countries not qualifying for benefits under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), the examiner should request removal of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bib-data sheet should include application number, country/intellectual property authority, day, month, and year of each foreign application claimed. Errors on oath/declaration or ADS require a new oath/declaration or ADS where appropriate; a petition for an unintentionally delayed priority claim may be required. Examiner must indicate on the bib-data sheet and in the Office action whether conditions of 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) have been met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page patent and CPA bib-data identification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The front page of a printed patent identifies prior applications for which benefits are claimed; for a patent issuing on a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), the front page will identify the application number and filing date of the most recent non-continued prosecution application in the chain (but not the filing date of the CPA) and all prior applications from which benefit was claimed in that most recent non-continued prosecution application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure bib-data sheet endorsement and front-page data accurately reflect the chain of benefit claims; corrections must be made via appropriate procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application status designations (new/rejected/amended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of application status: a 'new' application has not yet received examiner action; a 'rejected' application during prosecution and before allowance contains an unanswered examiner's action; an 'amended' status applies to applications with amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that an amendment filed prior to the first Office action does not alter 'new' status; RCE is not a type of new application filing. See relevant MPEP sections for procedural consequences.
